Characterization of bacterial host strains capable of tolerating process conditions (Task 6) Upon optimization of the full formaldehyde-to-GA bioconversion via FORCE pathways, we explored the capability of this system to produce a high concentration of products for a longer duration at a larger scale. To mitigate formaldehyde toxicity, we used paraformaldehyde as the substrate, which we found useful for a controlled supply of formaldehyde by changing the amount added to the media. The addition of 150 mM (4.5 g L–1) paraformaldehyde into the 50 mL resting-cell bioconversion resulted in close to full conversion of formaldehyde into GA within 24 h with a carbon yield of 94–95%, indicating no significant impact from the change of the substrate from formaldehyde solution to paraformaldehyde and a substantial scale up from 2 mL microtiter plates to 250 mL shake flasks (Figure 29C-D). As GA concentration increased in the media, pH control was shown necessary to maintain high productivity for a longer duration, while the culture with no pH control showed that the pH dropped as low as 4.8 from an initial pH of 7.2 (Figure 29D).
